prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: struggling to pay the mortgage. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 2)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a borrower says they are struggling with monthly payments, I check whether the issue is a short-term shock or a longer pattern, because that changes whether a temporary concession or a full affordability review is the right next step."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the difficulty is driven by rising essential bills rather than a change in income, I look closely at the surplus after essentials, because the payment pressure is often real even if the headline salary has not changed."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a case involves recent arrears, I do not assume the worst; I check how many payments were missed, whether they are now back on track, and whether the missed payments were linked to an identifiable event."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a member is already using credit to cover everyday spending, I treat that as a warning sign, because it can mean the mortgage is being supported by borrowing elsewhere rather than genuine affordability."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the borrower is open and early about difficulty, I prefer to capture a clear summary of their situation and any agreed action straight away, because uncertainty and repeated contact make stress and misunderstandings worse."},{"type":"observation","content":"When someone is struggling after a reduction in household income, I compare the current income to the long-term expected level, because the case may need a durable affordability solution rather than a temporary payment arrangement."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the mortgage is a remortgage and the monthly payment is about to rise, I check the new payment against the borrower’s day-to-day budget, because a case that looks fine at the offer stage can become unmanageable after completion."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a joint application becomes a single-income household, I reassess the whole file, because a change in household composition can turn a previously comfortable mortgage into a stretched one."},{"type":"preference","content":"When there is a credible sign of financial hardship, I prefer to gather the minimum extra information needed to make a fair decision, because asking for unnecessary detail can slow help and frustrate the member."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the member is worried about missing the next payment, I treat that as an urgent signal even if no arrears have formed yet, because early intervention is usually easier than managing arrears after they start."}]}
